## Why OpenSpec?

[](#why-openspec)

AI coding assistants are powerful but unpredictable when requirements live only in chat history. OpenSpec adds a lightweight spec layer so you agree on what to build before any code is written.

- **Agree before you build** — human and AI align on specs before code gets written

- **Stay organized** — each change gets its own folder with proposal, specs, design, and tasks

- **Work fluidly** — update any artifact anytime, no rigid phase gates

- **Use your tools** — works with 30+ AI assistants via skills

### How we compare

[](#how-we-compare)

**vs. [Spec Kit](https://github.com/github/spec-kit)** (GitHub) — Thorough but heavyweight. Rigid phase gates, lots of Markdown, Python setup. OpenSpec is lighter and lets you iterate freely.

**vs. [Kiro](https://kiro.dev)** (AWS) — Powerful but you're locked into their IDE and limited to Claude models. OpenSpec works with the tools you already use.

**vs. nothing** — AI coding without specs means vague prompts and unpredictable results. OpenSpec brings predictability without the ceremony.

## Updating OpenSpec

[](#updating-openspec)

**Upgrade the CLI**

With the standalone install, run `openspec install`. If you installed with npm:

```
npm install -g @fission-ai/openspec@latest
```

If you installed OpenSpec with Homebrew:

```
brew upgrade openspec
```

**Refresh agent instructions**

Run this inside each project to regenerate AI guidance and refresh the installed skills:

```
openspec update
```

## Usage Notes

[](#usage-notes)

**Model selection**: OpenSpec works best with high-reasoning models. We recommend Codex 5\.5 and Opus 4\.7 for both planning and implementation.

**Context hygiene**: OpenSpec benefits from a clean context window. Clear your context before starting implementation and maintain good context hygiene throughout your session.

# Set up your project

Add OpenSpec to a project: run init, see what it wrote, and adjust it.

Copy MarkdownOpen

## [Pick where OpenSpec lives](#pick-where-openspec-lives)Copy Anchor Link

- **In your repo (the default)**: specs and changes sit next to the code they describe and are versioned with it. The rest of this page follows this path.

- **In a store**: a separate planning repo shared by the repos that use it, for multi-repo setups or keeping planning out of the repo entirely. [Stores (beta)](/docs/stores) covers when that's worth it and how to set one up.

## [Initialize your project](#initialize-your-project)Copy Anchor Link

With the CLI installed ([Installation](/docs/installation)), run init at the root of your project. In your terminal:

Copy Text

```
cd <your-project>
openspec init
```

Init asks which AI tools you use, writes the workflow files for the ones you pick, and reports what you got:

Copy Text

```
OpenSpec Setup Complete

Created: Claude Code
6 skills in .agents/skills/ (linked from .claude/skills/)
Config: openspec/config.yaml (schema: spec-driven)
```

If your tool runs in an IDE, restart it so it picks up the new skills.

Re-running init is safe:

- Tools you already set up print `Refreshed` instead of `Created`.

- Running init again with a new tool selected adds that tool.

- The `--tools` flag skips the picker ([CLI reference](/docs/cli)).

### [Migrate an existing `project.md`](#migrate-an-existing-projectmd)Copy Anchor Link

Init does not copy legacy `openspec/project.md` into `config.yaml`. It keeps the file and prints an AI-assisted migration request.

In your AI chat:

Copy Text

```
Review openspec/project.md and migrate its useful content to openspec/config.yaml.
Keep context concise: include only project-wide facts needed during artifact creation, apply, and archive.
Move artifact-specific guidance into rules for the matching artifacts.
Move guidance for apply or archive into the matching operations entry.
Leave out generic, outdated, or verbose material. Do not delete project.md.
```

Review `config.yaml`, then delete `project.md` when ready.

## [What init installs](#what-init-installs)Copy Anchor Link

Running init creates two things in your project:

- An `openspec/` folder at the repo root

- Workflow files: skills in the shared `.agents/skills/` folder, with links from a tool's own folder where it needs them (`.claude/skills/`, for example)

Commit all of it like the rest of your source.

Init also removes the command files earlier versions generated, and keeps any you edited. A project set up before 1\.0 also has older leftovers: folders like `.claude/commands/openspec/`, and OpenSpec marker blocks in files like `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`. An interactive init asks before removing them. With `--force`, with `--tools`, or in a non-interactive run, init removes them without asking, including any edits inside those blocks, so back them up first.

### [The `openspec/` folder](#the-openspec-folder)Copy Anchor Link

Every OpenSpec artifact lives here, at the root of your project. Here's what that looks like:

Copy Text

```
openspec/
├── config.yaml     project settings and context for the AI
├── specs/          your specs (empty for now)
└── changes/        in-motion changes (empty for now)
    └── archive/    completed changes move here
```

[Project config](/docs/project-config) covers `config.yaml`.

### [The workflow files (skills)](#the-workflow-files-skills)Copy Anchor Link

These are the OpenSpec workflows, the actions you'll use as you work. Here they are as installed skills, in the shared `.agents/skills/` folder:

Copy Text

```
.agents/skills/
├── openspec-explore/              think through an idea first
├── openspec-propose/              propose a change
├── openspec-apply-change/         implement a change's tasks
├── openspec-update-change/        revise a change's plan
├── openspec-sync-specs/           sync a change's spec updates into specs/
├── openspec-archive-change/       move a finished change to the archive
├── openspec-verify-change/        check the implementation matches the plan (not included by default)
└── openspec-bulk-archive-change/  archive several changes at once (not included by default)
```

This is the default set plus two optional workflows. [Profiles](/docs/profiles) lists all twelve.

Each skill is written once, here, no matter how many tools you set up. A tool that doesn't read `.agents/skills/` (Claude Code, Kiro, and others) gets a link to each skill in its own folder, such as `.claude/skills/openspec-propose`. MiniMax Code is the one exception: its skills go to `~/.minimax/skills/` in your home folder. [Supported tools](/docs/supported-tools#where-skills-go) shows the layout and which tools get links.

Each workflow is a **skill**: instructions your agent picks up when you ask for the work, or that you invoke by name (`/openspec-apply-change` in Claude Code, `$openspec-apply-change` in Codex). [Supported tools](/docs/supported-tools#support-matrix) shows the spelling for each tool.

OpenSpec 1\.x also wrote a command file per workflow (`/opsx:apply`). OpenSpec 2\.0 installs skills only. [Upgrade to 2\.0](/docs/upgrade-to-2) covers what changes.

#### [Change what gets installed](#change-what-gets-installed)Copy Anchor Link

The interactive picker changes the workflow set ([Profiles](/docs/profiles)). In your terminal:

Copy Text

```
openspec config profile
```

Answering yes to "Apply changes to this project now?" applies it on the spot. Other projects pick it up on their next `openspec update`. The setting is global, per machine.

#### [Claude Code doesn't show the workflows](#claude-code-doesnt-show-the-workflows)Copy Anchor Link

Claude Code loads OpenSpec skills from `.claude/skills/openspec-*`, which link to `.agents/skills/openspec-*`. If they are missing, refresh the project. In your terminal:

Copy Text

```
openspec update
```

Restart Claude Code, then run `/openspec-propose` in its chat. If only some workflows are missing, [change your profile](/docs/profiles#expanding-the-set-optional-workflows).

Setup is done. The [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart) takes your first change from here.

## [openspec init](#openspec-init)Copy Anchor Link

Initializes OpenSpec in a project.

Copy Text

```
openspec init                        # current directory, interactive tool picker
openspec init --tools claude,cursor  # set up specific tools, no prompts
openspec init --tools none           # openspec/ structure only, no tool files
```

With no `--tools`, init prompts you to pick tools in an interactive terminal. Outside one, it sets up the tools it detects in the project. With none detected it exits 1 and lists the valid ids.

**Store-only repositories**

When `openspec/config.yaml` contains a `store:` line and the repo has no local specs or changes, run init from the repository root:

Copy Text

```
# install Claude Code integration files in the code repo
openspec init --tools claude
```

- **Integration files**: written in the code repo.

- **`openspec/config.yaml`**: preserved byte-for-byte.

- **`openspec/specs/` and `openspec/changes/`**: not created in the code repo.

Running init from a subdirectory exits 1 and tells you to run it from the repository root. `--language` also exits 1 because the language belongs in the external store's config. Run init in the store root or edit that config directly.

**Arguments**

| Argument | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `path` | The project directory to initialize. Default: current directory. Created if missing. |

**Options**

| Flag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--tools <tools>` | Comma-separated tool ids, `all`, or `none`. Skips the picker. Ids are listed in [Supported tools](/docs/supported-tools). |
| `--language <language>` | Add a language instruction to a new project config. Rejected when the repo's `store:` line points to an external store. |
| `--force` | Remove files from older OpenSpec layouts without asking. Interactive runs otherwise confirm the cleanup first. |
| `--profile <profile>` | Override the global config profile for this run: `core` (the standard workflow set) or `custom` (the workflows saved in global config). |
| `--no-animation` | Show a static welcome screen instead of the animated one. |

**Output**

OpenSpec writes its skills once, to `.agents/skills/`. Tools that need them get links in their own folder. MiniMax Code instead gets its own copy in `~/.minimax/skills/`:

Copy Text

```
▌ OpenSpec structure created
✔ Setup complete for Claude Code

OpenSpec Setup Complete

Created: Claude Code
6 skills in .agents/skills/ (linked from .claude/skills/)
Config: openspec/config.yaml (schema: spec-driven)

Getting started:
  Start your first change: /openspec-propose "your idea"
```

`--tools none` creates only `openspec/config.yaml`. On an already-initialized project, init rewrites the installed files in place and the summary reads `Refreshed: Claude Code` with `Config: openspec/config.yaml (exists)`.

**Exit codes**

- `0`: setup completed.

- `1`: invalid `--tools` or `--profile` value, a non-interactive run with no tools detected and no `--tools`, or an invalid store-only invocation.

## [openspec update](#openspec-update)Copy Anchor Link

Updates OpenSpec's installed instruction files.

Copy Text

```
openspec update             # refresh tools whose files are older than the CLI
openspec update --force     # rewrite files even when they're current
openspec update --dry-run   # list what an update would change, and change nothing
```

update finds the tools init configured and compares their generated files against the CLI's version. When a newer OpenSpec release exists, it first offers to upgrade the CLI, then reruns with the upgraded version. Set `OPENSPEC_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` to skip the check.

**Arguments**

| Argument | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `path` | The project directory to update. Default: current directory. |

**Options**

| Flag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--force` | Rewrite every configured tool's files even when they're up to date. |
| `--dry-run` | Report every file the update would add, change, or delete, and write nothing. No CLI upgrade check, no prompts. Combine with `--force` to preview a forced update. |
| `--json` | With `--dry-run`, print the plan as JSON. Without `--dry-run` it exits 1\. |

**Previewing an update**

`--dry-run` plans the update a non-interactive run would make: the same code path, with every write and delete recorded instead of performed. Every file the real update would touch is listed, including:

- moving OpenSpec files out of a tool's former directory (`.kimi/` to `.kimi-code/`, `.windsurf/` to `.devin/`, `.codex/` and `.agent/` to `.agents/`);

- saving the global config when an install from before profiles gets one;

- syncing the GitHub Copilot cloud agent files;

- with `--force`, setting up tools found only in legacy artifacts and cleaning those artifacts up, including retired global Codex prompts.

Copy Text

```
openspec update --dry-run
```

Copy Text

```
2 file(s) would change:
  update  .agents/skills/openspec-propose/SKILL.md  (openspec)
  add     ~/.config/openspec/config.json  (openspec)
```

`--dry-run --json` prints the same plan as one JSON document:

Copy Text

```
{
  "changes": [
    { "path": ".agents/skills/openspec-propose/SKILL.md", "action": "update", "tool": "openspec" },
    { "path": "~/.config/openspec/config.json", "action": "add", "tool": "openspec" }
  ],
  "notes": [],
  "failures": []
}
```

| Field | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `changes[].path` | Project-relative path. A file outside the project, such as a global skill or the global config, is shown from your home directory as `~/...`, or as an absolute path when it is outside home too. |
| `changes[].action` | `add`, `update`, or `delete`. A file whose new bytes match the old ones is not listed. |
| `changes[].tool` | The configured tool the file belongs to, such as `claude`. Files that belong to no one tool are `openspec`: the shared skills in `.agents/skills/`, the global config, and legacy-artifact cleanup. |
| `notes[]` | `{ code, message }` for a step a terminal user would be asked about or warned of. `legacy-tool-directories`: a move that an interactive run asks about first; `changes` lists it as made. `legacy-artifacts`: files from OpenSpec's older layout were found, such as `openspec-proposal.md` slash commands or OpenSpec marker blocks in `AGENTS.md`. Without `--force` a non-interactive update leaves them alone, so `changes` does too; `--dry-run --force` lists their cleanup. `edited-skills`: update will replace an edit you made inside a skill it installs, and the message names the files. Empty for an ordinary refresh. |
| `failures[]` | `{ tool, error }` for each tool the real update would fail on, including a write it cannot make: a directory where a file belongs, a file where a directory belongs, or a file or folder without write permission. For that tool, `changes` stops where the real update stops; the other tools are still planned. Failures the disk only reports while writing, such as running out of space, cannot be foreseen. |

A failure before planning, such as no OpenSpec directory, still prints exactly one JSON document: the empty plan plus a `status` array with `severity`, `code` (`update_error`), and `message`. The exit code is 1\.

**Output**

When every tool's files match the CLI version:

Copy Text

```
✓ All 1 tool(s) up to date (v1.7.0)
  Tools: claude

Use --force to refresh files anyway.
```

When a tool's files came from an older CLI (or with `--force`, which prints `Force updating 1 tool(s): claude` instead):

Copy Text

```
Updating 1 tool(s): claude (1.6.0 → 1.7.0)

✔ Updated Claude Code

✓ Updated: Claude Code (v1.7.0)
Tools: Claude Code
```

An update that touches an IDE-based tool, such as Cursor or Kiro, ends with `Restart your IDE to refresh skills.`

In a directory without OpenSpec, update refuses:

Copy Text

```
✖ Error: No OpenSpec directory found. Run 'openspec init' first.
```

**Exit codes**

- `0`: files updated, or everything already up to date.

- `1`: no OpenSpec directory at the path, or the update failed.

## [openspec config](#openspec-config)Copy Anchor Link

Views and changes global configuration.

Copy Text

```
openspec config list                  # see current settings
openspec config set profile core      # change one value
openspec config profile               # interactive workflow picker
```

| Subcommand | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `path` | Print the config file location. |
| `list` | Show all current settings. |
| `get <key>` | Print one value, raw and scriptable. |
| `set <key> <value>` | Set a value, coercing its type. |
| `unset <key>` | Remove a key so its default applies. |
| `reset` | Reset all configuration to defaults. |
| `edit` | Open the config file in `$EDITOR`. |
| `profile [preset]` | Configure which workflows are installed. |

Config is global to your machine, stored as JSON where `config path` points: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/openspec/config.json` if set, else `~/.config/openspec/config.json` (macOS, Linux) or `%APPDATA%\openspec\config.json` (Windows). Every subcommand accepts `--scope <scope>`, but only `global` works today. Any other scope exits 1 with `Error: Project-local config is not yet implemented`.

### [openspec config path](#openspec-config-path)Copy Anchor Link

Copy Text

```
openspec config path
```

Copy Text

```
/Users/you/.config/openspec/config.json
```

### [openspec config list](#openspec-config-list)Copy Anchor Link

Copy Text

```
openspec config list          # readable settings plus profile summary
openspec config list --json   # raw config as JSON
```

**Options**

| Flag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Print the config object as JSON. |

**Output**

Each setting, then a profile summary. It marks the profile as explicit or default and flags `delivery` as retired:

Copy Text

```
featureFlags: {}
profile: core
delivery: skills

Profile settings:
  profile: core (default)
  delivery: skills (retired in 2.0, ignored)
  workflows: propose, explore, apply, update, sync, archive (from core profile)
```

### [openspec config get](#openspec-config-get)Copy Anchor Link

Copy Text

```
openspec config get profile
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `key` | The key to read. Dots reach nested values (`featureFlags.workspaces`). |

**Output**

The bare value, ready for scripts. Objects print as compact JSON:

Copy Text

```
core
```

**Exit codes**

- `0`: value printed.

- `1`: key has no value, and nothing is printed.

### [openspec config set](#openspec-config-set)Copy Anchor Link

Copy Text

```
openspec config set profile core
openspec config set featureFlags.workspaces true
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `key` | The key to write, dotted for nested values. |
| `value` | The new value. `true`/`false` become booleans, numeric strings become numbers. |

**Options**

| Flag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--string` | Store the value as a string, skipping type coercion. |
| `--allow-unknown` | Permit keys the schema doesn't know. |

**Output**

Copy Text

```
Set featureFlags.workspaces = true
```

`delivery` is still accepted, so older scripts keep working, but it no longer changes anything ([Upgrade to 2\.0](/docs/upgrade-to-2)):

Copy Text

```
Set delivery = "skills"
Note: delivery no longer changes anything; OpenSpec 2.0 installs skills only.
```

Unknown keys and invalid values fail with exit 1 before anything is saved:

Copy Text

```
Error: Invalid configuration key "bogus.key". Unknown top-level key "bogus".
Use "openspec config list" to see available keys.
Pass --allow-unknown to bypass this check.
```

Copy Text

```
Error: Invalid configuration - profile: Invalid option: expected one of "core"|"custom"
```

If the config file exists but does not hold a JSON object, whether because it is not valid JSON at all or because its root is something else such as `null` or an array, `config set`, `config unset` and `config profile` exit 1 and leave the file unchanged. Fix it with `openspec config edit`, or replace it with `openspec config reset --all`:

Copy Text

```
Error: /home/you/.config/openspec/config.json could not be parsed, so it was left unchanged.
Fix it with "openspec config edit", or reset it with "openspec config reset --all".
```

Until it is fixed, telemetry and the background update check in `openspec update` stay off. An explicit `openspec version --check` still runs.

### [openspec config unset](#openspec-config-unset)Copy Anchor Link

Copy Text

```
openspec config unset profile
```

Removes the key so the default applies again. Keys with built-in defaults always count as set, so this reports success even if you never set them:

Copy Text

```
Unset profile (reverted to default)
```

A key with no value at all prints `Key "featureFlags.nothere" was not set`. Both cases exit 0\. A config file that cannot be parsed exits 1 instead, as for `config set`.

### [openspec config reset](#openspec-config-reset)Copy Anchor Link

Copy Text

```
openspec config reset --all      # asks for confirmation
openspec config reset --all -y   # no prompt
```

**Options**

| Flag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--all` | Required. Reset everything. |
| `-y, --yes` | Skip the confirmation prompt. |

**Output**

Copy Text

```
Configuration reset to defaults
```

Without `--all` it exits 1 and prints the usage line.

**Exit codes**

- `0`: reset done, or you answered no at the prompt.

- `1`: `--all` missing.

- `130`: prompt cancelled with Ctrl-C.

### [openspec config edit](#openspec-config-edit)Copy Anchor Link

Copy Text

```
openspec config edit
```

Opens the config file in `$EDITOR` (falling back to `$VISUAL`), creating it with defaults first if missing. When the editor closes, the file is validated. Invalid JSON or an invalid config exits 1\.

The editor value may carry arguments and quoted paths, for example `code --wait` or `"/Applications/Sublime Text.app/Contents/SharedSupport/bin/subl" -w`. It is split into words without a shell, so `$VAR`, `~` and `;` are passed through literally. An editor that cannot start, or exits non-zero, prints a one-line error and exits 1\.

With no editor configured it exits 1:

Copy Text

```
Error: No editor configured
Set the EDITOR or VISUAL environment variable to your preferred editor
Example: export EDITOR=vim
```

### [openspec config profile](#openspec-config-profile)Copy Anchor Link

Copy Text

```
openspec config profile        # interactive picker (needs a terminal)
openspec config profile core   # apply the core preset directly
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `preset` | Optional preset name. Only `core` exists. It selects the core workflows. |

With no preset, an interactive picker shows your current workflows, lets you change them (a checkbox list), prints the diff, and inside an OpenSpec project offers to run `openspec update` for you. Outside a terminal it exits 1:

Copy Text

~~~
Interactive mode required. Use `openspec config profile core` or set config via environment/flags.
~~~

**Output**

Changed config doesn't reach projects until they update:

Copy Text

~~~
Config updated. Run `openspec update` in your projects to apply.
~~~

**Exit codes**

- `0`: profile saved, or you kept current settings.

- `1`: unknown preset, no terminal, or the offered `openspec update` failed.

- `130`: picker cancelled with Ctrl-C.

## [openspec list](#openspec-list)Copy Anchor Link

Lists changes, or specs with `--specs`.

Copy Text

```
openspec list                    # active changes, most recently modified first
openspec list --archived         # archived changes
openspec list --all              # active and archived changes
openspec list --specs            # specs with requirement counts
openspec list --json             # machine-readable, includes the resolved root
```

Rows come from `openspec/changes/` and `openspec/specs/` under the resolved root. The default change listing skips `openspec/changes/archive/`.

**Options**

| Flag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--specs` | List specs instead of changes. |
| `--changes` | List changes. This is the default. |
| `--archived` | List only archived changes. Can't be combined with `--specs`. |
| `--all` | List active and archived changes. Can't be combined with `--specs`. Takes precedence over `--archived`. |
| `--sort <order>` | `recent` (last modified first) or `name`. Default: `recent`. Specs always sort by name. |
| `--json` | Print JSON instead of the table. |
| `--store <id>` | Use a registered store as the OpenSpec root instead of the current project. |

**Output**

One row per change: name, task status, last modified. The status column reads `No tasks`, `2/5 tasks`, or `✓ Complete`.

Copy Text

```
Changes:
  add-rate-limit     No tasks      just now
```

`--all` groups active and archived changes under separate headings. Each group uses the selected sort order:

Copy Text

```
Changes:
  add-rate-limit     No tasks      just now

Archived Changes:
  2026-08-10-add-login     ✓ Complete    2d ago
```

Copy Text

```
Specs:
  api     requirements 1
```

`--json` adds task counts and a `status` of `no-tasks`, `in-progress`, or `complete`:

Copy Text

```
{
  "changes": [
    {
      "name": "add-rate-limit",
      "completedTasks": 0,
      "totalTasks": 0,
      "lastModified": "2026-08-11T13:44:40.171Z",
      "status": "no-tasks"
    }
  ],
  "root": {
    "path": "/Users/you/projects/my-app",
    "source": "nearest"
  }
}
```

With `--archived` or `--all`, every change object includes an `archived` boolean. The combined array uses the selected sort order. An archived change can still have an `in-progress` status when its tracked task file has unchecked tasks. Without either flag, the JSON shape stays unchanged.

An empty listing prints `No active changes found.`, `No archived changes found.`, `No changes found.`, or `No specs found.` and still exits 0\.

A change is a directory directly under `openspec/changes/`. Unlike specs, changes cannot be nested in a namespace folder. A folder like `changes/mobile/` that only wraps a change (`changes/mobile/refresh-token/`) is listed with the status `not a change`, followed by a warning that names the nested directories. `--json` marks that entry with a `nested` array and adds a top-level `warnings` array. `show`, `status`, `validate` and `archive` refuse the folder with the same message. To fix it, move the change up and fold the namespace into its name:

Copy Text

```
mv openspec/changes/mobile/refresh-token openspec/changes/mobile-refresh-token
rmdir openspec/changes/mobile
```

**Exit codes**

- `0`: listing printed, even when empty.

- `1`: no OpenSpec root found (outside a project, no `--store`).

## [openspec show](#openspec-show)Copy Anchor Link

Prints a change or spec, as markdown or JSON.

Copy Text

```
openspec show add-rate-limit              # change: prints proposal.md
openspec show add-rate-limit --diff       # change: append requirement diffs
openspec show api                         # spec: prints spec.md
openspec show api --json --no-scenarios   # spec JSON without scenario text
```

With no name, show asks change or spec, then lists items to pick from. Outside an interactive terminal it exits 1 and prints the direct forms instead.

**Arguments**

| Argument | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `item-name` | The change or spec to show, by folder name (`add-rate-limit`, `api`). |

**Options**

| Flag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Print structured JSON instead of raw markdown. |
| `--type <change\|spec>` | Pick the type when a change and a spec share a name. |
| `--no-interactive` | Never prompt: a missing name becomes an error. |
| `--deltas-only` | JSON, change: restrict output to deltas. Change JSON is already delta-only, so output matches plain `--json`. |
| `--requirements-only` | Deprecated alias for `--deltas-only`. Warns on stderr. |
| `--diff` | Change: append per-requirement delta diffs. Ignored with a warning for specs. |
| `--requirements` | JSON, spec: keep requirement text, empty the `scenarios` arrays. |
| `--no-scenarios` | JSON, spec: same output as `--requirements`. |
| `-r, --requirement <id>` | JSON, spec: output one requirement by 1-based position. Can't combine with `--requirements`. |
| `--store <id>` | Use a registered store as the OpenSpec root instead of the current project. |

Flags that don't apply to the resolved type are ignored with a warning on stderr.

**Output**

Text mode is a raw passthrough: a change prints its `proposal.md`, a spec prints its `spec.md`.

Copy Text

```
# Add rate limiting

## Why
Unauthenticated clients can exhaust the API.

## What Changes
- Add per-client rate limiting to the public API.
```

For a change, `--diff` prints the proposal first, then a `Specifications Changed (diffs)` section. ADDED requirements include their full text. REMOVED requirements retain the authored Reason and Migration. RENAMED requirements show FROM and TO. MODIFIED requirements show a unified diff against the matching main requirement.

If a MODIFIED header matches only after folding case or whitespace, the output includes both the diff and a warning that archive matching is exact. If the main spec or requirement is missing, the output warns and prints the full delta block. A MODIFIED block with no textual difference prints `(no textual changes)`.

A change with `--json` is delta-shaped:

Copy Text

```
{
  "id": "add-rate-limit",
  "title": "Add rate limiting",
  "deltaCount": 1,
  "deltas": [
    {
      "spec": "api",
      "operation": "ADDED",
      "description": "Add requirement: The API SHALL limit each client to 100 requests per minute.",
      "requirement": {
        "name": "Rate limit",
        "text": "The API SHALL limit each client to 100 requests per minute.",
        "scenarios": [
          {
            "name": "Client exceeds the limit",
            "rawText": "- **WHEN** a client sends its 101st request within a minute\n- **THEN** the API responds 429"
          }
        ]
      },
      ...
    }
  ],
  "root": {
    "path": "/Users/you/projects/my-app",
    "source": "nearest"
  }
}
```

Each requirement carries its `name`, the header text after `Requirement:`. This is the name archive matches MODIFIED, REMOVED and RENAMED entries against. Each scenario carries its `name`, the header text after `Scenario:`. A closing `#` run on either header is not part of the name.

`--json --diff` keeps this top-level shape. A MODIFIED delta gains a `diff` string, a `warning` string, or both. Other operations are unchanged. An empty `diff` string means the main and delta blocks are textually identical.

A spec with `--json` lists its requirements with scenarios. Requirements and scenarios carry the same `name` fields as change JSON:

Copy Text

```
{
  "id": "api",
  "title": "api",
  "overview": "Public HTTP API behavior.",
  "requirementCount": 1,
  "requirements": [
    {
      "name": "Health endpoint",
      "text": "The API SHALL expose a health endpoint.",
      "scenarios": [
        {
          "name": "Health check succeeds",
          "rawText": "- **WHEN** a client requests GET /health\n- **THEN** the API responds 200"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "format": "openspec"
  },
  "root": {
    "path": "/Users/you/projects/my-app",
    "source": "nearest"
  }
}
```

An unknown name suggests near matches: `Unknown item 'does-not-exist'. Did you mean: add-rate-limit, api?`. A name that matches both a change and a spec errors and asks for `--type`.

**Exit codes**

- `0`: item printed.

- `1`: unknown or ambiguous name, no name outside a terminal, an out-of-range `-r` index, `--requirements` combined with `-r`, or a delta or main spec cannot be read for `--diff`.

## [openspec validate](#openspec-validate)Copy Anchor Link

Checks changes and specs for structural issues.

Copy Text

```
openspec validate add-rate-limit   # one change or spec, by name
openspec validate --all            # every change and spec
```

With no name and no bulk flag, validate prompts you to pick items. Outside an interactive terminal it exits 1 and prints the bulk flags instead.

**Arguments**

| Argument | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `item-name` | The change or spec to validate, by folder name (`add-rate-limit`, `api`). |

**Options**

| Flag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--all` | Validate every change and spec. |
| `--changes` | Validate every change. |
| `--specs` | Validate every spec. |
| `--archived` | Check task completion in archived changes, without validating their applied spec deltas. |
| `--strict` | Treat warnings as failures. |
| `--type <change\|spec>` | Pick the type when a change and a spec share a name. |
| `--json` | Print a structured report instead of text. |
| `--report <mode>` | Bulk output: `full` (default) or `findings`. Requires an explicit bulk scope. |
| `--concurrency <n>` | Max parallel validations in bulk runs. Default: `OPENSPEC_CONCURRENCY`, else 6\. |
| `--no-interactive` | Never prompt: a missing or ambiguous name becomes an error. |
| `--store <id>` | Use a registered store as the OpenSpec root instead of the current project. |

**Output**

Bulk runs print one status line per item, followed by any findings, and end with totals:

Copy Text

```
✓ change/add-rate-limit
✓ spec/api
Totals: 2 passed, 0 failed (2 items)
```

**Task checkbox findings**

Progress counts checkboxes and nothing else, so a task file written as plain bullets reads as zero tasks: `openspec list` and `openspec status` report no work, and `openspec archive` has nothing to flag as incomplete. Validate reports a `WARNING` on each tracked task file that lists work without a checkbox:

Copy Text

```
⚠ [WARNING] tasks.md: This change counts as 0 tasks: no line in its tracked task files is a checkbox, so "openspec list" and "openspec status" report no work and "openspec archive" has nothing to flag as incomplete. Write each task as "- [ ] 1.1 Description".
```

The warning fires only when the change's whole tracked set holds no checkbox at all. One file of prose beside a real checklist is not reported, and a change mid-authoring keeps its progress the moment a single checkbox exists. `--strict` turns the warning into a failure. The line number is in the `--json` report.

Fenced blocks, HTML comments, YAML front matter and indented code are not scanned, so a pasted terminal sample is never mistaken for a task list.

**Archive merge findings**

For changes, validate runs archive's merge builder against the current main specs without writing files. It reports merge conflicts, such as a missing `MODIFIED` target or a conflicting `ADDED` requirement, as `INFO`:

Copy Text

```
ℹ [INFO] api/spec.md: Archive would refuse this delta: api MODIFIED failed for header "### Requirement: Rate limiting" - not found
```

These findings appear even when validation passes, in both text and JSON output. `INFO` never changes the exit code, including under `--strict`: a missing target may belong to a sibling change that has not archived yet. Deltas already synced into the main specs follow archive's existing merge rules.

This check does not run archive's later merged-spec validation or retirement checks. A clean report does not guarantee that archive will succeed.

If the merge preflight cannot start, an `INFO` finding explains why. Existing validation findings and the exit code stay unchanged.

A failing item lists each issue and the fix:

Copy Text

```
Change 'add-rate-limit' has issues
✗ [ERROR] api/spec.md: ADDED "Rate limiting" must include at least one scenario
Next steps:
  - Ensure change has deltas in specs/: use headers ## ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED/RENAMED Requirements
  - Each requirement MUST include at least one #### Scenario: block
  - Debug parsed deltas: openspec show add-rate-limit --json --deltas-only
```

`--json` prints one report for the run:

Copy Text

```
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "add-rate-limit",
      "type": "change",
      "valid": true,
      "issues": [],
      "durationMs": 2
    }
  ],
  "summary": {
    "totals": {
      "items": 1,
      "passed": 1,
      "failed": 0
    },
    "byType": {
      "change": {
        "items": 1,
        "passed": 1,
        "failed": 0
      }
    }
  },
  "version": "1.0",
  "root": {
    "path": "/Users/you/projects/my-app",
    "source": "nearest"
  }
}
```

`issues` entries carry a `level` of `ERROR`, `WARNING`, or `INFO`.

**Exit codes**

- `0`: every validated item passed, including an empty bulk scope.

- `1`: an item failed, the report request is invalid, `openspec/config.yaml` cannot be read or is not valid YAML, or the run failed (for example an unknown name or no OpenSpec root). A config that cannot be read or parsed stops the run before any item is checked; with `--json` it is reported as a single `status` entry with the code `unreadable_config` or `unparseable_config`.

### [\--report full\|findings](#--report-fullfindings)Copy Anchor Link

Selects the output for an explicit bulk validation scope:

- **`full`**: every item. This is the default. Explicit `--report full` keeps the existing output shape without adding report metadata.

- **`findings`**: only items with issues, including passing items with warnings or information. Every item is still validated. Totals, strict-mode behavior, and exit codes are unchanged.

Copy Text

```
openspec validate --all --report findings
openspec validate --archived --report findings --json
```

**Scopes**

| Flags | Findings `report.scope` |
| --- | --- |
| `--all` | `all` |
| `--changes` | `changes` |
| `--specs` | `specs` |
| `--changes --specs`, or `--all` with either flag | `all` |
| `--archived` | `archived` |

Both explicit report modes reject a positional item name, a missing bulk scope, or archive and active scopes combined.

#### [Findings text output](#findings-text-output)Copy Anchor Link

**Human output**: stdout prints `Scope: <scope> (<count> items)`, then totals. With no issue-bearing items:

Copy Text

```
Scope: all (2 items)
No item findings.
Totals: 2 passed, 0 failed (2 items)
```

Issue-bearing item labels, severity labels, paths, and messages print to stderr. Active-scope failures keep the `Details:` rerun hint after totals. The existing root banner and progress output may precede the report.

#### [Findings JSON output](#findings-json-output)Copy Anchor Link

`--report findings --json` prints one document. This example has two clean items:

Copy Text

```
{
  "report": {
    "kind": "validation-findings",
    "version": "1.0",
    "scope": "all",
    "returnedItems": 0,
    "totalItems": 2
  },
  "itemFindings": [],
  "summary": {
    "totals": { "items": 2, "passed": 2, "failed": 0 },
    "byType": {
      "change": { "items": 1, "passed": 1, "failed": 0 },
      "spec": { "items": 1, "passed": 1, "failed": 0 }
    }
  },
  "root": { "path": "/Users/you/projects/my-app", "source": "nearest" }
}
```

- **`report.kind` and `report.version`**: identify the `validation-findings` shape, version `1.0`. There is no top-level `version` or `items`.

- **`report.returnedItems` and `report.totalItems`**: count the returned records and all validated items, respectively.

- **`itemFindings`**: complete item records whose `issues` array is nonempty. Includes `ERROR`, `WARNING`, and `INFO` issues. Each record retains `id`, `type`, `valid`, `issues`, and `durationMs`. Archived items use `type: "change"`.

- **`summary`**: full-run totals and per-type counts, not counts of the returned subset. An empty scope has zero totals and exits 0\.

- **`root`**: the same selected-root metadata as the full report.

**Record preservation**: returned items keep their full-report order and any additive fields on items or issues. Filtering does not rewrite messages or locations, including optional `line` and `column` fields.

**Command failures**: root-selection or item-discovery failures retain the existing `status` diagnostic and exit 1\. They do not return a completed findings report or a successful empty report.

#### [Invalid report requests](#invalid-report-requests)Copy Anchor Link

Both explicit report modes reject these requests before root selection or item discovery:

- An unsupported report value, including an empty string.

- A positional item name, even with a bulk flag.

- No explicit bulk scope.

- `--archived` combined with `--all`, `--changes`, or `--specs`.

In JSON mode, a rejected request exits 1 with only a single-element `status` array. It has no `root` or report payload:

Copy Text

```
openspec validate --all --report bogus --json
```

Copy Text

```
{
  "status": [
    {
      "severity": "error",
      "code": "invalid_validation_report_request",
      "message": "Unknown validation report 'bogus'.",
      "fix": "Use --report full|findings with --all, --changes, --specs, or --archived, without an item name. Do not combine archived and active scopes."
    }
  ]
}
```

Human mode prints the error to stderr. A bare `--report` with no value is a Commander syntax error on stderr, including with `--json`; it does not use this diagnostic envelope.

#### [Filter a full report externally](#filter-a-full-report-externally)Copy Anchor Link

For a custom JSON view, filter the full report with `jq` or PowerShell. These script examples preserve the validation exit code and leave command-error documents intact.

In Bash with `jq`:

Copy Text

```
if validation_json=$(openspec validate --all --json); then
  validation_exit=0
else
  validation_exit=$?
fi
printf '%s\n' "$validation_json" |
  jq 'if has("items") then .items |= map(select(.issues | length > 0)) else . end'
exit "$validation_exit"
```

In PowerShell:

Copy Text

```
$validationJson = openspec validate --all --json
$validationExit = $LASTEXITCODE
$validationReport = $validationJson | ConvertFrom-Json
if ($validationReport.PSObject.Properties.Name -contains 'items') {
  $validationReport.items = @($validationReport.items | Where-Object { $_.issues.Count -gt 0 })
}
$validationReport | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 100
exit $validationExit
```

These custom views keep the full report's keys but omit clean items. They are neither complete full-v1 reports nor the versioned `--report findings` shape.

## [openspec archive](#openspec-archive)Copy Anchor Link

Moves a completed change to the archive and updates the main specs.

Copy Text

```
openspec archive add-rate-limit -y                # archive one change, merge its deltas
openspec archive add-rate-limit -y --skip-specs   # archive without touching the specs
```

With no name, archive prompts you to pick a change. Outside an interactive terminal it exits 1 and prints the rerun command instead.

**Arguments**

| Argument | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `change-name` | The change to archive, by folder name (`add-rate-limit`). |

**Options**

| Flag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `-y, --yes` | Answer yes to every confirmation: spec updates, incomplete tasks, skipped validation. |
| `--skip-specs` | Archive without touching the main specs (infrastructure, tooling, or doc-only changes). |
| `--no-validate` | Skip validation. Archive asks you to confirm first, and `-y` answers it. |
| `--json` | Print a structured result instead of text. Needs `--yes` to confirm spec updates. |
| `--store <id>` | Use a registered store as the OpenSpec root instead of the current project. |

**Output**

A successful run reports task status, previews the spec updates, applies them, and names the archive folder:

Copy Text

```
Task status: ✓ Complete

Specs to update:
  api: update
Applying changes to openspec/specs/api/spec.md:
  + 1 added
Totals: + 1, ~ 0, - 0, → 0
Specs updated successfully.
Change 'add-rate-limit' archived as '2026-08-11-add-rate-limit'.
```

The change folder moves whole to `openspec/changes/archive/2026-08-11-add-rate-limit/`, today's date prefixed to its name. Each delta merges into its main spec: the ADDED requirement above was appended to `openspec/specs/api/spec.md`. Without `-y`, archive shows the preview and asks before updating. Declining still archives the change and leaves the specs alone.

With `--json --yes`:

Copy Text

```
{
  "archive": {
    "change": "add-rate-limit",
    "archivedAs": "2026-08-11-add-rate-limit",
    "path": "/Users/you/projects/my-app/openspec/changes/archive/2026-08-11-add-rate-limit",
    "specsUpdated": true,
    "totals": {
      "added": 1,
      "modified": 0,
      "removed": 0,
      "renamed": 0
    }
  },
  "root": {
    "path": "/Users/you/projects/my-app",
    "source": "nearest"
  }
}
```

Archive validates the change first and refuses one that fails:

Copy Text

```
Validation errors in change delta specs:
  ✗ ADDED "Rate limiting" must include at least one scenario

Validation failed. Please fix the errors before archiving.
To skip validation (not recommended), use --no-validate flag.
```

Incomplete tasks warn but don't block. Interactively archive asks whether to continue, and `-y` continues on its own:

Copy Text

```
Task status: 1/2 tasks
Warning: 1 incomplete task(s) found. Continuing due to --yes flag.
```

**Exit codes**

- `0`: the change was archived, with or without spec updates.

- `1`: validation failed, the change name is unknown, or a confirmation was needed and no answer could be read.

Reports artifact completion status for one change or every active change.

Copy Text

```

openspec status --change add-rate-limit --json   # structured report
openspec status --all                            # every active change
openspec status --all --json                     # one batch report
```

When active changes exist, use exactly one of `--change` or `--all`. Without either, status exits 1 and lists the available changes, even when only one exists:

Copy Text

```

  add-rate-limit
```

When the project has no active changes, status prints `No active changes. Create one with: openspec new change <name>` and exits 0 even without either flag. With `--all --json`, the same empty state is `{ "changes": [], "message": "No active changes.", "root": ... }`.

**Options**

| Flag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--change <id>` | The change to report on, by folder name. |
| `--all` | Report every active change, sorted by name. Can't be combined with `--change`. |
| `--schema <name>` | Override the schema auto-detected from `openspec/config.yaml`. An unknown name is an error. |
| `--json` | Print a structured report instead of text. |
| `--store <id>` | Use a registered store as the OpenSpec root instead of the current project. |

**Output**

A checklist of the schema's artifacts: `[x]` done, `[ ]` ready to write, `[-]` blocked until the artifacts it depends on exist.

Copy Text

```

Schema: spec-driven
Change root: /Users/you/projects/my-app/openspec/changes/add-rate-limit

[x] proposal
[x] specs
[ ] design
[-] tasks (blocked by: design)

Copy Text

[x] specs
[x] design
[x] tasks

All planning artifacts complete!
Next: openspec instructions apply --change "add-rate-limit" --json
```

`--json` adds per-artifact dependencies, resolved file paths, and a suggested next step. Trimmed:

Copy Text

```
{
  "changeName": "add-rate-limit",
  "schemaName": "spec-driven",
  "isComplete": false,
  "nextSteps": [
    "Run openspec instructions design --change \"add-rate-limit\" --json before writing that artifact."
  ],
  "artifacts": [
    {
      "id": "proposal",
      "outputPath": "proposal.md",
      "status": "done",
      "requires": []
    },
    {
      "id": "design",
      "outputPath": "design.md",
      "status": "ready",
      "requires": [
        "proposal"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "tasks",
      "outputPath": "tasks.md",
      "status": "blocked",
      "requires": [
        "specs",
        "design"
      ],
      "missingDeps": [
        "design"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

With `--all --json`, `changes` contains the same status object for each change, without a per-change `root`. The selected root appears once on the envelope. This example trims the per-change status fields shown above:

Copy Text

```
{
  "changes": [
    {
      "changeName": "add-rate-limit",
      "schemaName": "spec-driven",
      "artifacts": []
    }
  ],
  "root": {
    "path": "/Users/you/projects/my-app",
    "source": "nearest"
  }
}
```

**Exit codes**

- `0`: every requested status printed; an empty `--all` report also exits 0\.

- `1`: a requested change failed to load, `--change` or `--all` is missing, the two flags were combined, the change doesn't exist, or the schema override is unknown.

- Analizar el proyecto Vue en `D:\proyectos\vue-bs\sms` y prepararlo para SDD/OpenSpec, generando documentación base y ahora inicializando OpenSpec.

## Requirements
- Entregar `project-context.md`, specs base de 2–3 módulos en `specs/_baseline/` y `AGENTS.md`.
- Preparar el proyecto para comenzar a usar OpenSpec sin romper el código existente.
- Documentación limpia, ordenada y directa, en español.

## Decisions
- Se crearon 3 specs base: autenticación/sesión, configuración/directorio y mensajería SMS.
- Se documentó el estado AS-IS, no el deseado, con reglas numeradas `R-*` y criterios de aceptación.
- Se decidió integrar OpenSpec con la estructura oficial `openspec/config.yaml`, `openspec/specs/`, `openspec/changes/`, y skills en `.agents/skills/`.
- No se modificó código fuente; solo documentación.

## Work State
### Completed
- Análisis completo del repo: stack, arquitectura, rutas, stores, API, convenciones y reglas de negocio.
- Creado `project-context.md` (contexto persistente global).
- Creado `AGENTS.md` (reglas operativas y flujo SDD/OpenSpec).
- Creado `specs/_baseline/README.md` (índice, invariantes globales, protocolo de cambio).
- Creados `specs/_baseline/01-auth-sesion.md`, `02-configuracion-directorio.md`, `03-mensajeria-sms.md`.
- Verificado estado git: solo archivos nuevos sin commit (`?? AGENTS.md`, `?? project-context.md`, `?? specs/`).
- Verificado que el CLI `openspec` no está instalado; `node v24.15.0`; `npm.cmd 11.12.1` y `npx.cmd 11.12.1` funcionan (npm.ps1 bloqueado por ExecutionPolicy).
- Consultada documentación oficial de OpenSpec 2.0: instalación, `openspec init --tools <ids>`, estructura y comandos.

### Active
- Preparar la inicialización real de OpenSpec en el repo.

### Blocked
- El CLI `openspec` no está instalado; hay que instalarlo o ejecutarlo vía `npx.cmd`.

## Next Move
1. Instalar OpenSpec con `npm.cmd install -g @fission-ai/openspec@latest` o usar `npx.cmd @fission-ai/openspec@latest`.
2. Ejecutar `openspec init --tools <id>` de forma no interactiva; determinar el ID correcto para OpenCode (revisar `https://openspec.dev/docs/supported-tools`) o usar `--tools none` y crear skills manualmente.
3. Crear `openspec/config.yaml` con contexto conciso del proyecto (stack, arquitectura, convenciones, comandos).
4. Migrar/duplicar las specs base a `openspec/specs/<módulo>/spec.md` en formato OpenSpec (`## Purpose`, `## Requirements`, `### Requirement:`, `#### Scenario:`).
5. Crear `openspec/changes/archive/` y verificar con `openspec list --specs`, `openspec validate --all`, `openspec view`.
6. Actualizar `AGENTS.md` y `project-context.md` para que apunten a `openspec/` como fuente de verdad y a `specs/_baseline/` como referencia histórica.
7. Confirmar si se debe commitear o dejar los cambios sin commit.

## Relevant Files
- `D:\proyectos\vue-bs\sms\project-context.md`: contexto global del stack/arquitectura/convenciones.
- `D:\proyectos\vue-bs\sms\AGENTS.md`: reglas para agentes y flujo SDD/OpenSpec.
- `D:\proyectos\vue-bs\sms\specs\_baseline\README.md`: índice e invariantes globales.
- `D:\proyectos\vue-bs\sms\specs\_baseline\01-auth-sesion.md`: spec base de auth.
- `D:\proyectos\vue-bs\sms\specs\_baseline\02-configuracion-directorio.md`: spec base de configuración.
- `D:\proyectos\vue-bs\sms\specs\_baseline\03-mensajeria-sms.md`: spec base de mensajería.
- `D:\proyectos\vue-bs\sms\package.json`: scripts y dependencias.
- `D:\proyectos\vue-bs\sms\vite.config.ts`: plugins/alias/auto-imports.
- `D:\proyectos\vue-bs\sms\src\router\index.ts`: rutas y guards.
- `D:\proyectos\vue-bs\sms\src\api\client\client.ts`: Axios e interceptores.
- `D:\proyectos\vue-bs\sms\src\lib\query-keys.ts`: claves Pinia Colada.

## Important Context
- OpenSpec 2.0 instala skills en `.agents/skills/`; `openspec init --tools none` crea solo `openspec/config.yaml`.
- Estructura esperada: `openspec/config.yaml`, `openspec/specs/`, `openspec/changes/`, `openspec/changes/archive/`.
- Comandos útiles: `openspec init`, `openspec list --specs`, `openspec validate --all`, `openspec view`, `openspec new change <name>`, `openspec archive <name> -y`.
- OpenSpec exige Node.js >= 22.12.0; el entorno tiene v24.15.0.
- En Windows usar `npm.cmd`/`npx.cmd` porque `npm.ps1` está bloqueado por ExecutionPolicy.
- No hay tests en el repo; `npm run typecheck` y `npm run build_sms` son la verificación mínima.
- Riesgo conocido: `index.html` referencia `/src/main.js`, pero el archivo real es `src/main.ts`.
- No se ha ejecutado `typecheck`/`build` porque solo se añadieron documentos.

# Supported tools

Which AI coding tools OpenSpec supports, and how to invoke each one's skills.

Copy MarkdownOpen

Every tool in the matrix runs the same OpenSpec workflows, installed as skills. Earlier versions also wrote command files. [Upgrade to 2\.0](/docs/upgrade-to-2) covers what happens to them.

## [Where skills go](#where-skills-go)Copy Anchor Link

Every tool's skills are written once, to `.agents/skills/`. A tool that doesn't read that folder gets one link per skill in its own `skills/` folder, pointing back at the shared copy.

A project set up for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex:

Copy Text

```
my-project/
├── .agents/skills/
│   ├── .openspec-target           the tools set up here, one per line
│   └── openspec-propose/SKILL.md  the one copy every tool reads
└── .claude/
    └── skills/openspec-propose    link to ../../.agents/skills/openspec-propose
```

Cursor and Codex read `.agents/skills/` themselves, so they need nothing else.

`.openspec-target` is how `openspec update` knows what is OpenSpec's. Each line is one of:

| Line | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `<tool>` | A tool set up in this project, such as `cursor`. |
| `<tool> own-files` | OpenSpec gave the tool links in its own folder, such as `claude own-files`. Delete that folder and `update` removes the tool. |
| `keep <skill>` | Your own skill, such as `keep openspec-mine`. It was there before OpenSpec used the folder, so OpenSpec never touches it. |

- **Links**: Claude Code, Continue, ForgeCode, Kiro, CodeBuddy, EasyCode, iFlow, CodeArts, Lingma, GigaCode, Veai, Rovo Dev, Code Studio, and Hermes Agent.

- **No link**: every other tool reads `.agents/skills/` directly, so it never loads a skill twice.

- **Where a link can't be made**: OpenSpec writes a plain copy instead, and refreshes it on `openspec update`.

To add a tool that isn't listed, see [Link another tool](#link-another-tool).

## [Link another tool](#link-another-tool)Copy Anchor Link

A tool that reads `.agents/skills/` needs nothing: pick `agents` at init ([Other / Universal](#other--universal-shared-agents-skills)). A tool that reads only its own folder can be pointed at the shared copy with one link. In your terminal, from the project root:

Copy Text

```
mkdir -p .mytool
ln -s ../.agents/skills .mytool/skills
```

On Windows, in Command Prompt:

Copy Text

```
mkdir .mytool
mklink /J .mytool\skills .agents\skills
```

Replace `.mytool` with your tool's folder. If the tool already has a `skills/` folder of its own, link each skill instead: `ln -s ../../.agents/skills/openspec-propose .mytool/skills/openspec-propose`.

**Committing links**: Git stores links as links. A teammate on Windows should run `git config --global core.symlinks true` (or clone with `git clone -c core.symlinks=true <url>`) and enable Developer Mode so links can be created. Otherwise each link checks out as a small text file, which `openspec update` replaces with a plain copy of the skill. A junction made with `mklink /J` is not committed as a link; recreate it on each machine.

## [Per-tool notes](#per-tool-notes)Copy Anchor Link

A tool not listed here behaves exactly as its row reads.

### [Amazon Q Developer (retired)](#amazon-q-developer-retired)Copy Anchor Link

OpenSpec 2\.0 no longer supports Amazon Q Developer: it can't load skills, and AWS is retiring it in favor of Kiro. `openspec init --tools amazon-q` stops with that message. In a project set up for it, `openspec update` removes the prompts and skills OpenSpec wrote in `.amazonq/`, and keeps and lists any you edited. Set up Kiro instead: `openspec init --tools kiro`.

### [Antigravity](#antigravity)Copy Anchor Link

- **Current folder**: Antigravity v1.20.5 and later read workspace skills and workflows from `.agents/`.

- **Legacy folder**: after OpenSpec writes replacements, it removes equivalent generated files from `.agent/`. Custom files and changed generated files stay in `.agent/` for you to review.

- **Shared skills**: Antigravity reads the same `.agents/skills/` copy as every other tool. Workflows OpenSpec wrote to `.agents/workflows/` before 2\.0 are removed on update.

### [Cline](#cline)Copy Anchor Link

Skills are the shared copy in `.agents/skills/`. Workflows OpenSpec wrote to `.clinerules/workflows/` before 2\.0 are removed on update; your own rules there are left alone.

### [Codex](#codex)Copy Anchor Link

- **CLI and IDE extension**: mention `$openspec-propose` with your idea, or run `/skills` to select the skill. Codex does not recognize `/openspec-propose` ([upstream issue](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/11817)).

- **Desktop app**: open Skills in the sidebar and select `openspec-propose`. [OpenAI's skills documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills) describes both interfaces.

- **Shared folder**: Codex reads the same `.agents/skills/` copy as every other tool. Skills name each other by skill name (`openspec-apply-change`), which Codex invokes as `$openspec-apply-change`.

- **Legacy path**: skills installed under `.codex/skills/` by older versions are migrated on the next `openspec update`.

### [DeepSeek Harness](#deepseek-harness)Copy Anchor Link

- **Project root**: DSH uses the nearest `.git` ancestor, or the current directory outside Git. Run `openspec init --tools dsh` there. For a nested OpenSpec project, add the absolute path to its `.agents/skills/` directory to DSH's `customSkillDirs`. Git-root skills still win if names overlap ([upstream discovery rules](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/tree/master/packages/skill/skill-filesystem)).

- **Old copies**: a `.dsh/skills/` copy from before 2\.0 would take precedence over `.agents/skills/`. `openspec update` removes untouched ones and reports any you changed.

### [Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)](#devin-desktop-formerly-windsurf)Copy Anchor Link

- **Both agents**: Devin Desktop and Devin Local both run the shared skills. Workflows OpenSpec wrote to `.devin/workflows/` before 2\.0 are removed on update.

- **Rename**: `--tools windsurf` still resolves to `devin`. A project holding OpenSpec files in the legacy `.windsurf/` folder is offered the move on the next `openspec update`.

### [GitHub Copilot](#github-copilot)Copy Anchor Link

- **Skills**: Copilot loads `.agents/skills/openspec-*/SKILL.md`. Invoke a skill as `/openspec-<skill>`. In the CLI, if a skill disappears while its file still exists, run `/skills reload`, then `/skills info openspec-propose` to confirm discovery. In an IDE, restart it.

- **Old prompt files**: the `.github/prompts/opsx-*.prompt.md` files OpenSpec wrote before 2\.0 are removed on update.

### [GSD](#gsd)Copy Anchor Link

- **Project skills**: GSD reads OpenSpec workflows from [`.agents/skills/`](https://github.com/open-gsd/gsd-pi/blob/main/docs/user-docs/skills.md).

- **Invocation**: ask GSD to use the `openspec-<workflow>` skill. GSD can also select a matching skill through its skill discovery setting.

- **No subagent files**: [`.gsd/agents/`](https://github.com/open-gsd/gsd-pi/blob/main/docs/user-docs/subagents.md) contains GSD subagent definitions. OpenSpec does not write workflow skills there.

### [Hermes Agent](#hermes-agent)Copy Anchor Link

OpenSpec links each skill into the project's `.hermes/skills/` folder. Hermes v2026.6.5 and later load that folder once you trust the repo: run `hermes skills trust` inside the project. Until then, Hermes shows a notice that it found project skills but did not load them. On older versions, add the project's `.hermes/skills/` folder to `skills.external_dirs` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` instead. Init prints this reminder after install.

### [MiniMax Code](#minimax-code)Copy Anchor Link

- **Global only**: skills go to `~/.minimax/skills/`. Nothing is written inside the repo.

### [Warp](#warp)Copy Anchor Link

- **What OpenSpec claims**: nothing in `.warp/`. Warp settings and `WARP.md` are not created or edited.

### [Other / Universal (shared `.agents` skills)](#other--universal-shared-agents-skills)Copy Anchor Link

- **When it fits**: any tool that reads the shared `.agents/skills/` folder, including tools with no row in the matrix. It is the entry to pick when your assistant is not listed. The init picker's search box finds it by `universal`, `other`, `generic`, `custom`, `proprietary`, `unlisted`, `unsupported`, `vendor-neutral`, or `agents.md`.

- **Alongside other tools**: every tool reads this one skill tree. `.openspec-target` lists the tools set up in the project. To remove a tool, delete its folder (or, for a tool with no folder of its own, its line in `.openspec-target`).

- **Your own `openspec-*` skills**: a skill already in `.agents/skills/` before OpenSpec used the folder is kept, never written over, and recorded as `keep <skill>` in `.openspec-target`. Delete that skill to let OpenSpec write its own.

- **What OpenSpec claims**: only the `openspec-*` folders and the `.openspec-target` list. Anything else under `.agents/` is left alone.

- **`AGENTS.md`**: not created or edited. The target is the `.agents/` folder, not the file.

1: # Spec Base — Autenticación y sesión
2: 
3: | Campo | Valor |
4: |---|---|
5: | Módulo | `auth` |
6: | Estado | AS-IS (comportamiento actual) |
7: | Rutas | `/auth/*`, `/index`, `/home` |
8: | Archivos clave | `src/stores/auth/*`, `src/api/auth.ts`, `src/router/index.ts`, `src/views/auth/*`, `src/components/features/app/AppIdle.vue`, `src/main.ts` |
9: 
10: ---
11: 
12: ## 1. Propósito
13: 
14: Permitir el acceso de usuarios internos de ETECSA a la SPA mediante sesión por cookie, proteger las rutas privadas, cerrar sesión, expirar la sesión por inactividad y permitir que usuarios autorizados “personifiquen” a otro usuario.
15: 
16: ---
17: 
18: ## 2. Actores y permisos
19: 
20: | Actor | Capacidades |
21: |---|---|
22: | Visitante | Ver login; autenticarse. |
23: | Usuario autenticado | Acceder a `/index`, `/sms`, `/configurar`; cerrar sesión. |
24: | Usuario con `can_impersonate` | Buscar usuarios y personificar. |
25: | Usuario personificado (`is_impersonating`) | Usar la app como el usuario objetivo; puede volver a personificar. |
26: | Administrador (`admin: true`) | Ver la opción “Usuarios” en Configurar. La autorización real la aplica el backend. |
27: 
28: > El frontend **no** implementa RBAC completo: solo oculta navegación. No asumir que ocultar una opción equivale a denegar acceso.
29: 
30: ---
31: 
32: ## 3. Rutas
33: 
34: | Path | Name | Meta | Comportamiento |
35: |---|---|---|---|
36: | `/auth/login` | `auth-login` | `logout` | Login. `props.next` navega a `route.query.next` o `/home`. |
37: | `/auth/logout` | `auth-logout` | `logout` | Página de sesión terminada. |
38: | `/auth/expired` | `auth-expired` | `logout` | Sesión expirada; `beforeEnter` agrega `next=from.fullPath`. `props.next` navega a `route.query.next`. |
39: | `/auth/impersonate` | `auth-impersonate` | `requiresAuth` | Búsqueda y personificación. |
40: | `/index` | `index` | `requiresAuth` | Home autenticado. |
41: | `/home` | `home` | — | Alias `/`; redirige a `/index`. |
42: 
43: ---
44: 
45: ## 4. Componentes y stores
46: 
47: ### Vistas
48: 
49: - `src/views/auth/index.vue` — layout de auth.
50: - `src/views/auth/login.vue` — formulario usuario/contraseña, alerta inline de credenciales inválidas.
51: - `src/views/auth/logout.vue` — confirmación visual de cierre.
52: - `src/views/auth/expired.vue` — aviso y botón “Continuar trabajando”.
53: - `src/views/auth/impersonate.vue` — buscador y listas de usuarios.
54: - `src/components/features/auth/impersonate/UserCard.vue`, `UsersList.vue`.
55: 
56: ### Stores / composables
57: 
58: | Archivo | Responsabilidad |
59: |---|---|
60: | `src/stores/auth/useAuthQuery.ts` | `GET /auth/login`; usuario actual; `staleTime: Infinity`. |
61: | `src/stores/auth/useLogin.ts` | `POST /auth/login`; guarda el usuario en la caché de Colada. |
62: | `src/stores/auth/useLogout.ts` | `DELETE /auth/login`; setea el usuario a `null` en caché. |
63: | `src/stores/auth/useImpersonate.ts` | `POST /auth/impersonate/{userId}`; recarga la ventana. |
64: | `src/stores/auth/useImpersonateQuery.ts` | Búsqueda de usuarios con `search.length >= 2`; marca `actual`. |
65: | `src/composables/useAuthUserMenu.ts` | Acciones del menú de usuario; visibilidad de “Personificar”. |
66: | `src/components/features/app/AppIdle.vue` | Temporizador de inactividad y heartbeat. |
67: | `src/main.ts` | Evento global `unauthorized` → redirección a login. |
68: 
69: ### Endpoints
70: 
71: | Método | Endpoint | Uso |
72: |---|---|---|
73: | `POST` | `/auth/login` | Autenticación con `{ username, password }`. |
74: | `GET` | `/auth/login` | Usuario actual (chequeo de sesión). |
75: | `DELETE` | `/auth/login` | Logout. |
76: | `POST` | `/auth/impersonate/{userId}` | Personificar. |
77: | `GET` | `/auth/users?search=` | Usuarios personificables. |
78: | `GET` | `/auth_groups/auth_groups` | Catálogo de roles/grupos (usado en usuarios). |
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: ## 5. Flujos actuales
83: 
84: ### 5.1 Arranque y guard de rutas
85: 
86: 1. `router.beforeEach` detecta `meta.requiresAuth`.
87: 2. Espera a que `isPending` de `useAuthQuery` sea `false` (`until(isPending).toBe(false)`).
88: 3. Si `authUser` es `null`, redirige a `{ name: 'auth-login', query: { next: to.fullPath } }`.
89: 4. Si hay usuario, continúa.
90: 
91: ### 5.2 Login
92: 
93: 1. `validate()` exige `username` y `password` no vacíos.
94: 2. `useLogin().mutateAsync(credentials)` → `POST /auth/login`.
95: 3. En éxito, `queryCache.setQueryData(queryKeys.auth.user(), () => data)`.
96: 4. La vista ejecuta `props.next()`.
97: 5. En fallo, el error se muestra inline en `BAlert` (“Credenciales no válidas”); **no** se emite toast global para el intento de login.
98: 
99: ### 5.3 Logout
100: 
101: 1. `router.afterEach` detecta `meta.logout` y, si hay usuario, ejecuta `useLogout()`.
102: 2. `DELETE /auth/login`.
103: 3. En éxito, el usuario en caché se setea a `null`.
104: 4. La ruta `auth-logout` muestra “Sesión terminada por el usuario”.
105: 
106: ### 5.4 401 global
107: 
108: 1. El interceptor Axios detecta `401`.
109: 2. Si **no** es la ruta de login, emite `error` (toast “Tu sesión ha expirado”).
110: 3. Si **no** es un intento de login (`POST /auth/login`), emite `unauthorized`.
111: 4. `main.ts` escucha `unauthorized` y, si no estamos ya en `auth-login`, hace:
112:    `router.push({ name: 'auth-login', query: { next: currentRoute.fullPath } })`.
113: 5. Se lanza `AuthenticationError`.
114: 
115: ### 5.5 Expiración por inactividad (`AppIdle`)
116: 
117: - `timeout = 1440` minutos (24 h).
118: - `warning = 0.7` → overlay a los 1008 min (16.8 h).
119: - `LISTENERS = timeout / 3` → a los 480 min (8 h) empieza a escuchar `mousemove`, `mousedown`, `keydown`, `touchstart`.
120: - Cada acceso al servidor (`lastServerAccess`) reinicia el temporizador.
121: - Al hacer heartbeat, se ejecuta `refetch` de `GET /auth/login`.
122: - Al cumplirse el timeout, `stop()` y emite `expired` → `router.push({ name: 'auth-expired' })`.
123: - La página `auth-expired` permite “Continuar trabajando” y navega a `next` (la ruta previa).
124: 
125: ### 5.6 Personificación
126: 
127: 1. Visible si `authUser.can_impersonate` o `authUser.is_impersonating`.
128: 2. El buscador solo consulta con `search.length >= 2`.
129: 3. `useImpersonateQuery` marca `actual: d.id === authUser.id`.
130: 4. `useImpersonate().mutate(userId)` → `POST /auth/impersonate/{userId}`.
131: 5. En éxito, `window.location.reload()`.
132: 6. Mientras `is_impersonating`, el menú muestra “Personificado”.
133: 
134: ---
135: 
136: ## 6. Reglas de negocio actuales
137: 
138: | ID | Regla |
139: |---|---|
140: | `R-AUTH-01` | La sesión se transporta por cookie; no hay token en `localStorage` ni en headers manuales. |
141: | `R-AUTH-02` | Toda ruta con `meta.requiresAuth` exige usuario autenticado antes de renderizar. |
142: | `R-AUTH-03` | Un `401` en `POST /auth/login` **no** redirige ni muestra toast global; se muestra inline en el formulario. |
143: | `R-AUTH-04` | Un `401` en `GET /auth/login` (chequeo inicial) **no** muestra toast global. |
144: | `R-AUTH-05` | Un `401` en cualquier otra llamada redirige a login preservando `next`. |
145: | `R-AUTH-06` | Entrar a una ruta con `meta.logout` estando autenticado dispara logout en el servidor. |
146: | `R-AUTH-07` | La sesión expira a los 1440 min de inactividad; hay aviso visual al 70%. |
147: | `R-AUTH-08` | La actividad del usuario solo reinicia el temporizador después de 1/3 del timeout; antes de eso el temporizador corre aunque haya actividad. |
148: | `R-AUTH-09` | El heartbeat de sesión es `GET /auth/login`; cada respuesta del servidor también reinicia el temporizador. |
149: | `R-AUTH-10` | Personificar requiere `can_impersonate` o estar ya personificando; tras personificar se recarga toda la aplicación. |
150: | `R-AUTH-11` | `admin: true` es la única condición de UI para mostrar “Usuarios” en Configurar. |
151: | `R-AUTH-12` | `registration_key === 'blocked'` se muestra como “Bloqueado”; el bloqueo efectivo lo aplica el backend. |
152: | `R-AUTH-13` | El login declara que el usuario pertenece al dominio `etecsa.cu`; no hay validación local del dominio. |
153: | `R-AUTH-14` | El registro de usuarios no es público: solo un administrador crea usuarios. |
154: 
155: ---
156: 
157: ## 7. Contrato de datos usado por el frontend
158: 
159: ### Usuario autenticado (`authUser`)
160: 
161: | Campo | Tipo | Uso |
162: |---|---|---|
163: | `id` | `number \| string` | Comparación con usuario personificado. |
164: | `name` | `string` | Nombre visible en menú; comparación de autor de mensaje. |
165: | `username` | `string` | Mostrado en menú. |
166: | `admin` | `boolean` | Mostrar opción Usuarios. |
167: | `can_impersonate` | `boolean` | Mostrar/buscar personificación. |
168: | `is_impersonating` | `boolean` | Etiqueta “Personificado”. |
169: 
170: ### Credenciales
171: 
172: ```ts
173: interface LoginCredentials {
174:   username: string
175:   password: string
176: }
177: ```
178: 
179: ### Errores
180: 
181: - `AuthenticationError` (`401`), `AuthorizationError` (`403`), `NetworkError`, `ServerError`.
182: - Guardas: `isApiError`, `isNetworkError`, `isValidationError`.
183: 
184: ---
185: 
186: ## 8. Criterios de aceptación AS-IS
187: 
188: - **AC-AUTH-01** Dado un visitante sin sesión, al entrar a `/configurar/grupos` es redirigido a `/auth/login?next=/configurar/grupos`.
189: - **AC-AUTH-02** Con credenciales válidas, el login guarda el usuario y navega a `next` o `/home`.
190: - **AC-AUTH-03** Con credenciales inválidas, se muestra la alerta inline y no se navega.
191: - **AC-AUTH-04** Al entrar a `/auth/logout` con sesión, se ejecuta `DELETE /auth/login` y se limpia el usuario.
192: - **AC-AUTH-05** Tras 24 h sin actividad, se navega a `auth-expired` y se ofrece continuar.
193: - **AC-AUTH-06** Un `401` en una llamada de negocio redirige a login conservando la ruta actual en `next`.
194: - **AC-AUTH-07** Un usuario con `can_impersonate` puede buscar desde 2 caracteres y personificar; la app se recarga.
195: - **AC-AUTH-08** Un usuario sin `admin` no ve la opción “Usuarios”.
196: 
197: ---
198: 
199: ## 9. Límites y deuda conocida
200: 
201: - No hay refresh token ni renovación silenciosa; la sesión depende de la cookie del backend.
202: - El guard espera la query de auth, pero no revalida permisos por ruta.
203: - La personificación usa `window.location.reload()` y pierde estado de UI.
204: - `staleTime: Infinity` en `useAuthQuery` implica que el usuario en caché no se refresca salvo por login/logout/heartbeat/refetch explícito.
205: - No hay tests de auth.
206: - No se valida el dominio `etecsa.cu` en el cliente.

189: ## 6. Reglas de negocio actuales
190: 
191: ### 6.1 Grupos
192: 
193: | ID | Regla |
194: |---|---|
195: | `R-GRP-01` | Un grupo tiene `nombre` obligatorio; `apodo`, `label` y `descripcion` son opcionales. |
196: | `R-GRP-02` | La jerarquía se expresa con `pertenece` (id del padre). Si es `null` o el padre no existe, el grupo es raíz. |
197: | `R-GRP-03` | El árbol se construye en el frontend con `flatToTree(data, { parentKey: 'pertenece' })`; el backend devuelve lista plana. |
198: | `R-GRP-04` | Crear un subgrupo desde el detalle envía `pertenece = padreId`. |
199: | `R-GRP-05` | `label === 'origen'` identifica grupos seleccionables como origen de SMS (icono verde). El resto usa icono amarillo. |
200: | `R-GRP-06` | Las consultas de notificables/orígenes filtran por `label` con valores `grupo,centro` y `centro,origen`; el backend interpreta esos filtros. |
201: | `R-GRP-07` | Eliminar un grupo elimina permanentemente el grupo, sus grupos hijos y los suscriptores de esos grupos (según el texto de confirmación). |
202: | `R-GRP-08` | El detalle muestra tabs General, Grupos, Suscriptores y Notificados; Grupos/Suscriptores/Notificados son `lazy`. |
203: | `R-GRP-09` | La lista de grupos usa `RootTree` + `TreeNode` con indentación por nivel y estado activo/descendiente activo. |
204: | `R-GRP-10` | El alta/edición de grupo no permite elegir `pertenece` desde el formulario general; el padre se fija por la ruta de creación de hijos. |
205: 
206: ### 6.2 Suscriptores
207: 
208: | ID | Regla |
209: |---|---|
210: | `R-SUS-01` | `nombre` es obligatorio. |
211: | `R-SUS-02` | `telefono` es obligatorio y debe cumplir `MOVIL_PATRON = /^(\+53\|53)?\d{8}$/`. |
212: | `R-SUS-03` | `correo` es opcional; si existe, debe cumplir `EMAIL_PATRON`. |
213: | `R-SUS-04` | `grupo` es obligatorio en el alta/edición global. En el alta desde un grupo, se precarga `grupo = grupoId` y no se valida en el cliente. |
214: | `R-SUS-05` | `activo` por defecto es `true`; se muestra “Sí/No” y en la lista con icono verde/rojo. |
215: | `R-SUS-06` | `suplente` es opcional y se elige de la lista completa de suscriptores. |
216: | `R-SUS-07` | Eliminar un suscriptor conserva los registros históricos asociados (según el texto de confirmación). |
217: | `R-SUS-08` | El detalle de suscriptor muestra `grupo`, `suplente`, `modified_by` y `modified_on`; en edición se usan `grupo_id` y `suplente_id` del detalle. |
218: 
219: ### 6.3 Usuarios
220: 
221: | ID | Regla |
222: |---|---|
223: | `R-USR-01` | `first_name`, `last_name` y `username` son obligatorios. |
224: | `R-USR-02` | `grupos` es un arreglo de ids de `auth_groups`; se edita con checkboxes. |
225: | `R-USR-03` | `registration_key` solo se edita en el formulario de edición: `null` = Activo, `'blocked'` = Bloqueado. |
226: | `R-USR-04` | El alta no expone `registration_key`; el usuario nace activo por defecto. |
227: | `R-USR-05` | La lista marca en rojo y con icono `UserX` a los usuarios con `registration_key === 'blocked'`. |
228: | `R-USR-06` | Eliminar un usuario elimina también sus mensajes enviados (según el texto de confirmación). Se sugiere bloquear en lugar de eliminar. |
229: | `R-USR-07` | La opción “Usuarios” solo se muestra si `authUser.admin` es verdadero. |
230: | `R-USR-08` | El detalle muestra `first_name + last_name`, `username`, roles de `grupos`, estado de `registration_key`, `modified_by/on`. |
231: | `R-USR-09` | El catálogo de roles (`auth_groups`) usa `staleTime: Infinity`. |
232: 
233: ### 6.4 Plantillas
234: 
235: | ID | Regla |
236: |---|---|
237: | `R-PLT-01` | `texto` es obligatorio. |
238: | `R-PLT-02` | La búsqueda de plantillas es server-side (`?search=`). |
239: | `R-PLT-03` | En el compositor, el widget de plantillas solo busca con `search.length >= 2`. |
240: | `R-PLT-04` | Insertar una plantilla **concatena** su texto al cuerpo actual; no lo reemplaza. |
241: | `R-PLT-05` | Guardar plantilla desde el compositor crea una plantilla con el texto actual. |
242: | `R-PLT-06` | Eliminar una plantilla es permanente. |
243: 
244: ### 6.5 Notificados
245: 
246: | ID | Regla |
247: |---|---|
248: | `R-NOT-01` | “Notificados” de un grupo es el conjunto de grupos que reciben sus notificaciones, guardado en `grupo_b` (arreglo de ids). |
249: | `R-NOT-02` | La edición reemplaza el conjunto completo: `PUT /notificados/notificados/{grupoId}` con `{ grupo_b: [...] }`. |
250: | `R-NOT-03` | El árbol de selección usa `GET /grupos/grupos?label=grupo,centro` y permite marcar cualquier grupo. |
251: | `R-NOT-04` | La consulta de notificados de un grupo usa `GET /notificados/notificados?origen={grupoId}`. |
252: | `R-NOT-05` | No hay validación local de que `grupo_b` no esté vacío. |
253: 
254: ### 6.6 Patrones transversales de configuración
255: 
256: | ID | Regla |
257: |---|---|
258: | `R-CFG-01` | Toda operación de escritura invalida las listas correspondientes; las actualizaciones invalidan además los detalles. Las eliminaciones normalmente solo invalidan listas. |
259: | `R-CFG-02` | Los errores 422 se reflejan en `errorState` del formulario; los demás ya se notifican globalmente. |
260: | `R-CFG-03` | Tras crear, se navega al detalle del nuevo recurso usando el `id` devuelto. |
261: | `R-CFG-04` | Los modales de edición/eliminación se cierran con `back`; tras eliminar, con `forward` a la lista. |
262: | `R-CFG-05` | No se hace borrado optimista: primero responde el servidor y luego se invalida la caché. |

342: ## 8. Criterios de aceptación AS-IS
343: 
344: - **AC-CFG-01** Crear un grupo sin nombre muestra “Este campo no puede estar vacío” y no llama al backend.
345: - **AC-CFG-02** Un grupo creado desde “hijos/crear” aparece como hijo del grupo actual y se envía con `pertenece`.
346: - **AC-CFG-03** Eliminar un grupo muestra la advertencia de cascada (grupo, hijos y suscriptores) antes de ejecutar.
347: - **AC-CFG-04** Crear un suscriptor con teléfono inválido muestra “Formato no válido” y no envía.
348: - **AC-CFG-05** Un suscriptor sin correo es válido.
349: - **AC-CFG-06** Crear un usuario exige nombre, apellidos y username; los grupos son opcionales.
350: - **AC-CFG-07** Editar un usuario permite cambiar `registration_key` a Activo/Bloqueado.
351: - **AC-CFG-08** La lista de usuarios muestra en rojo a los bloqueados.
352: - **AC-CFG-09** Crear una plantilla sin texto muestra error local.
353: - **AC-CFG-10** En el compositor, el buscador de plantillas no consulta hasta escribir 2 caracteres.
354: - **AC-CFG-11** Guardar notificados de un grupo reemplaza `grupo_b` y refresca las listas/detalles.
355: - **AC-CFG-12** Un 422 del backend se muestra en los campos correspondientes del formulario.
